# FFmpeg, the part that plays Bink movies

The game's intro and credits are Bink 1 movies (`bink/intro.bik`,
`bink/credits.bik` on the disc). RAD's Bink SDK is proprietary, so the Apple
builds decode them with [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/)'s Bink demuxer and
decoders, through `port/runtime/bink_decoder.c`.

FFmpeg is licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1
or later (`COPYING.LGPLv2.1`, `LICENSE.md`). The rest of this repository is
CC0; this folder is not. Every file here keeps its own license header.
`libavutil/avsscanf.c` carries musl's MIT notice in place of the LGPL one.

## What is here

- **Release:** FFmpeg `n9.0.2` (`VERSION` has the tag and its commit).
- **Files:** 234, 3.3 MB, listed in `FILES.txt`; the 84 that are compiled are
  listed in `SOURCES.txt`, and the rest are headers and files those include.
- **Unmodified:** every file under `libavcodec/`, `libavformat/`, `libavutil/`
  and `compat/` is byte for byte the release's. There are no patches.
- **Generated by FFmpeg's `configure`,** not written by hand: `config.h`,
  `config_components.h`, `libavutil/avconfig.h`, `libavutil/ffversion.h` and
  the `*_list.c` files. `config.h` records the configure command in
  `FFMPEG_CONFIGURATION` and the license it results in in `FFMPEG_LICENSE`.
- **Ours:** `README.md`, `refresh.py`, `FILES.txt`, `SOURCES.txt`, `VERSION`.

The configuration enables the `bink` demuxer and the `bink`, `binkaudio_rdft`
and `binkaudio_dct` decoders and nothing else: no other codecs or formats, no
protocols, no filters, no libswscale or libswresample, no assembly, no
threads, no network, no external libraries. It does not pass `--enable-gpl`,
`--enable-version3` or `--enable-nonfree`, so configure reports "LGPL version
2.1 or later" and `refresh.py` refuses any other result, and any file whose
header is GPL-only.

The file list is not chosen by hand. `refresh.py` builds FFmpeg's three
libraries with that configuration, links `port/ios/tests/bink_probe.c`
against them and takes the objects the linker used, with every file those
were compiled from, and the public headers `bink_decoder.c` includes. Most of `libavutil` is here because FFmpeg's public API
needs it (options, frames, buffers, pixel and sample format tables), not
because Bink does.

## Building

`port/ios/CMakeLists.txt` compiles `SOURCES.txt` into the app when
`HALO_BINK` is on (the default; `tools/ios_build.py --bink off` turns it
off). With it off, none of this folder is compiled or linked, the app
carries no FFmpeg license file, and the game skips its movies as it did
before. `tools/bink_test.py` builds the same sources for the Mac and decodes
the player's own intro.

FFmpeg's objects are linked statically into the app's executable. The LGPL
lets a recipient of the app replace the library with a modified one and
relink; the app's own source, this folder and the build scripts are all in
this repository, so `tools/ios_build.py` rebuilds the app with whatever is
in this folder.

## Refreshing

```bash
git clone --depth 1 --branch n9.0.2 https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg.git /tmp/ffmpeg
python3 port/third_party/ffmpeg-bink/refresh.py /tmp/ffmpeg
python3 tools/bink_test.py
```

Use another release tag to move to it. The script cleans and configures the
checkout, so give it one of its own. It replaces everything here but the
files listed under "Ours", and rewrites `FILES.txt`, `SOURCES.txt` and
`VERSION`. Then update the release and the counts above, and the versions in
`NOTICE.md` and `port/ios/THIRD_PARTY.md`.

The generated `config.h` comes from a Mac. The iOS, tvOS, visionOS and Mac
Catalyst builds all use it: with assembly off it describes a generic CPU, and
the C library features it names are the same on Apple's platforms.
